best_narrative.headline: Zocdoc: Telehealth Competitors Mobilize Federal Lobbying on Access Economics
best_narrative.body: Zocdoc operates a healthcare directory and marketplace connecting patients to telehealth providers, creating material exposure to consumer protection and state medical advertising rules that govern how telehealth services compete for patient attention. Four competing telehealth operators filed federal lobbying disclosures between May 2025 and May 2026 on telehealth access and prescription economics, signaling industry-wide mobilization around regulatory and reimbursement pressures. New York, California, and Texas each maintain distinct advertising and anti-kickback enforcement regimes that govern how platforms market telehealth services and structure provider relationships. The government affairs team should monitor whether rival platforms are coordinating on state-level messaging or federal advocacy that could reshape competitive dynamics around telehealth visibility and patient acquisition.

best_narrative.headline: Spring Health: Competitors File Federal Telehealth Lobbying Push
best_narrative.body: Spring Health operates as a pure-play mental health platform embedded in employer benefits workflows, making state behavioral health licensing and Medicaid reimbursement shifts material operational exposures. Industry-standard regulatory exposures for this business model include state-level telehealth prescribing restrictions, asynchronous behavioral health licensing requirements, and employer plan mandate compliance. Two major competitors have filed federal lobbying disclosures on telehealth regulatory topics as of April 2026, signaling heightened attention to interstate licensing harmonization and reimbursement policy. Your government affairs team should monitor New York, California, and Florida for licensing reciprocity proposals that could accelerate or constrain employer-sponsored mental health access.
